q: For delay in completion of a work, liquidated damages are proposed to be levied on the contractor aggregating more than one-tenth of the contract value. Such a levy is not sustainable because the total liquidated damages under a works contract cannot exceed:

options.A: 10% of the contract value
options.B: 5% of the contract value
options.C: 15% of the contract value
options.D: 25% of the contract value

q: During the execution of a work, the contractor is adjudged insolvent and enters into an arrangement with his creditors. In this situation, the Railway may:

options.A: Continue the contract on the same terms in all cases
options.B: Transfer the contract automatically to his creditors
options.C: Suspend all his payments permanently without terminating the contract
options.D: Determine (terminate) the contract in accordance with the General Conditions of Contract

q: On a work, the quantity of an item actually executed turns out to be considerably different from the quantity provided for that item in the contract. In contract terminology, such a difference between the contracted quantities and the quantities actually executed is termed a:

options.A: Material modification
options.B: Vitiation of the contract
options.C: Deviation
options.D: Substituted item

q: A large work is divided into sections with stipulated intermediate milestones, and the contractor fails to achieve one of the milestones although the work is still in progress. As provided in the contract, liquidated damages in such a contract may be levied:

options.A: Only for delay in the final completion of the whole work
options.B: Also for failure to achieve the stipulated intermediate milestones, as provided in the contract
options.C: Only after the expiry of the maintenance period of the work
options.D: At twice the normal rate for each milestone delayed

q: An application by a contractor for extension of the period of completion of a work should ordinarily be made:

options.A: Before the expiry of the stipulated date of completion of the work
options.B: At any time within one year after the completion of the work
options.C: Only after the final bill of the work has been paid
options.D: To the tender committee which recommended the tender

q: A railway project which does not satisfy the normal test of financial remunerativeness may still be sanctioned when:

options.A: The contractor executing it agrees to bear the loss on the project
options.B: Its cost happens to be below the powers of sanction of the General Manager
options.C: It is justified on strategic or socio-economic considerations and is approved by the competent authority on those grounds
options.D: It is included in the Pink Book as a token work

q: A socially desirable project is not financially viable for private participation on its own, and the Government provides a capital grant to make it viable for a private partner. Such capital support or grant in a public-private partnership project is known as:

options.A: A loan taken by the contractor from a bank for the project
options.B: The difference between the estimated cost and the tendered cost of a work
options.C: Funding arranged by the contractor through his own equity
options.D: Viability Gap Funding (VGF)

q: Which of the following best describes the purpose for which Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL) was set up by the Railways?

options.A: To undertake and execute rail infrastructure projects, including through project-specific special purpose vehicles and mobilisation of extra-budgetary resources
options.B: To manufacture rolling stock for the Railways
options.C: To carry on the catering services on trains
options.D: To maintain the accounts of the zonal railways

q: For a major railway project, environmental clearance is required before the execution of the project can be taken up. The responsibility for obtaining such statutory clearances, as part of the processing of the project, rests with:

options.A: The contractor, after the award of the work
options.B: The project authority, i.e. the Railways
options.C: The tender committee which examined the tenders
options.D: The State Pollution Control Board on its own

q: At the close of a work, the executive proposes that the contractor's performance be left unrecorded. This is not in order because, on completion of a work, the performance of the contractor:

options.A: Is not required to be recorded anywhere
options.B: Is evaluated by the contractor himself
options.C: Is evaluated and recorded, and unsatisfactory performance can lead to action such as downgrading or banning from future tenders
options.D: Is considered only for the purpose of releasing the security deposit

q: For a proposed new line, the first-stage survey combining a broad engineering examination of the possible alignments with an assessment of the traffic expected on the line is the reconnaissance survey, abbreviated as:

options.A: RETS — Reconnaissance Engineering-cum-Traffic Survey
options.B: PETS — Preliminary Engineering-cum-Traffic Survey
options.C: FLS — Final Location Survey
options.D: RTS — Reconnaissance Traffic Statement

q: A zonal railway finances part of a project from Extra Budgetary Resources (Institutional Finance) — EBR(IF). Such resources are raised mainly:

options.A: From the Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: From the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: By levy of a cess on passengers
options.D: Through the Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC) by way of market borrowings

q: For computing the quantities of earthwork executed on a work, the executive relies on the levels recorded for the work in the:

options.A: Works Register maintained for the work
options.B: Level Book (field book) maintained for the work
options.C: Contractor's Ledger maintained in the accounts office
options.D: Comparative statement of the tenders received

q: A petty work of small value is executed and completed in a single operation, so that no running payments to the contractor are called for. Payment for such a work may be made through:

options.A: A secured advance bill
options.B: A mobilisation advance
options.C: A first and final bill
options.D: A percentage-rate bill

q: A firm seeks enlistment as a railway works contractor so that it may be considered for works up to a certain value. Enlistment or registration of contractors for railway works is done:

options.A: In different classes according to the monetary value of works they are eligible to undertake
options.B: For one work only at a time
options.C: Only if they are government departments
options.D: Without any classification, on a single common list

q: A proposal is made to insure a railway building with a commercial insurer. As a general rule, such insurance of Government (Railway) property is not resorted to because:

options.A: Insurance of government property is prohibited by the Railways Act, 1989
options.B: Contractors insure all railway property in every case
options.C: The assets of the Railways have no insurable value
options.D: The Government bears its own risks (self-insurance), and commercial insurance of its property is generally not considered economical

q: Before tenders for a work are invited, the Notice Inviting Tender (NIT) is published. Apart from a brief description of the work, the notice ordinarily indicates:

options.A: Only the name of the work
options.B: Its estimated cost, earnest money, period of completion and the due date and time for submission and opening of tenders
options.C: The rates at which the work will be awarded
options.D: The names of the contractors who will submit tenders

q: At the proposal stage, a rough cost estimate for a station building is required quickly, without detailed measurement of items. Such an approximate (rough cost) estimate is commonly prepared on the basis of:

options.A: Detailed measurement of each item of work
options.B: The rates quoted by contractors for similar buildings
options.C: The plinth area of the building multiplied by the plinth area rate
options.D: The cost of an old building without any adjustment

q: The prices of labour and materials have risen since the Unified Standard Schedule of Rates (USSOR) was issued for a railway. The rates in the USSOR are kept current by:

options.A: Revising them with reference to cost indices reflecting changes in the prices of labour and materials
options.B: Adopting the rates quoted by the lowest tenderers from time to time
options.C: Revising them only when a new Works Programme is prepared
options.D: Leaving them unchanged once they are issued

q: A tenderer preparing his bid for an item-rate work refers to the Schedule of Quantities (Bill of Quantities) in the tender documents. That schedule shows:

options.A: Only the total estimated cost of the work
options.B: The measurements recorded after completion of the work
options.C: The names of the approved contractors for the work
options.D: The items of work with their descriptions, units and approximate quantities, against which the tenderers quote their rates

q: A supplier claims Class-I local supplier status under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order in a procurement. He qualifies as a Class-I local supplier only if the local content of his goods, services or works is:

options.A: 20 per cent
options.B: 50 per cent or more
options.C: 75 per cent
options.D: 100 per cent

q: A station building work comprises civil construction together with electrical and signalling components, all to be executed together by a single agency. The tender invited for such a work is a:

options.A: Composite tender
options.B: Zonal tender
options.C: Percentage-rate tender
options.D: Single tender

q: Owing to an event beyond the control of either party, the performance of a works contract becomes impossible. Under the doctrine of frustration, embodied in Section 56 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, the consequence is that:

options.A: The contractor must complete the work at his own cost in all cases
options.B: The Railway must pay the full contract value to the contractor
options.C: The contract becomes void
options.D: The period of completion stands extended indefinitely

q: A contractor claims interest for the period for which his earnest money and security deposit remained with the Railways under a contract. The claim is not tenable because, in respect of such amounts:

options.A: Interest is payable to the contractor at the bank rate
options.B: Interest is payable only on the security deposit
options.C: Interest is payable if the work is completed before time
options.D: No interest is payable by the Railways for the period the amounts remain with them

q: A contract is determined on account of the contractor's default. For the portion of the work already executed by him before the determination, the position is that it is:

options.A: Ignored, and no payment is made for it
options.B: Measured and valued at the contract rates, and payment made for it subject to the recoveries and dues of the Railways
options.C: Paid for at the schedule of rates current in that year
options.D: Paid for only after the balance work is completed by another agency

q: A work has been completed in accordance with the contract and a certificate recording that fact is to be issued. The completion certificate for the work is issued by:

options.A: The Engineer-in-charge of the work
options.B: The contractor executing the work
options.C: The Accounts Officer of the division
options.D: The Railway Board

q: A track renewal work has just been completed on a running line. Until the renewed track consolidates, trains are initially allowed over the renewed portion:

options.A: At the maximum permissible speed straightaway
options.B: Only after one year of the completion of the work
options.C: Under a temporary speed restriction (caution order), which is relaxed progressively as the track consolidates
options.D: Only during the day time

q: In the bill for an earthwork item, different rates are applied for ordinary soil, hard soil and rock. This is because, for the purpose of measurement and payment, earthwork in a works contract is classified according to:

options.A: The season in which the work is executed
options.B: The nature of the soil or strata encountered, with separate rates for each class
options.C: The type of contract under which the work is executed
options.D: The designation of the officer recording the measurements

q: Earth required for forming an embankment on a work is obtained from excavations made at approved places, generally outside the formation. Such excavations are known as:

options.A: Trial pits
options.B: Ballast pits
options.C: Cable trenches
options.D: Borrow pits

q: A works contractor is found paying his workmen wages below the statutory floor fixed for the employment concerned. He is bound to pay to the workmen engaged by him wages not less than:

options.A: The minimum wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act, 1948 for the employment concerned
options.B: The wages demanded by the workmen
options.C: Half of the wages paid to regular railway staff for similar work
options.D: The wages prevailing in his home district

q: The alignment of a railway project passes through forest land which has to be diverted for the work. Before such diversion, the project authority is required to:

options.A: Occupy the land on payment of a nominal fee to the forest department
options.B: Obtain the permission of the local panchayat only
options.C: Obtain prior approval for the diversion under the Forest (Conservation) Act and bear the cost of compensatory afforestation and the net present value of the forest land diverted
options.D: Plant trees within the railway land in lieu of the forest land

q: Departmental charges are recovered from an outside body on a deposit work executed by the Railways for that body. In the railway accounts, the amount so recovered is:

options.A: Retained by the executing division as its own funds
options.B: Credited to the earnings (revenue receipts) of the Railways
options.C: Deposited in the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: Refunded to the party on completion of the work

q: One zonal railway executes a work on behalf of another railway, and the cost of the work has to be adjusted between the two railways. Such adjustment is effected through:

options.A: The Contractor's Ledger
options.B: The Stores Suspense account
options.C: The Traffic Book of the railways
options.D: Inter-Railway Financial Adjustment (IRFA)

q: To protect railway land from encroachment, the arrangement maintained by the Railways is:

options.A: Land plans and records, with the boundaries of railway land demarcated on the ground by boundary pillars or stones
options.B: No records of land at all
options.C: Only the completion reports of works executed on the land
options.D: A register of the contractors who have worked on the land

q: Two works tenders of widely different values are under consideration for acceptance. The authority competent to accept each of them is determined with reference to:

options.A: The designation of the officer who prepared the estimate
options.B: The number of tenderers who participated in the tender
options.C: The value of the tender, in accordance with the Schedule of Powers
options.D: The period allowed for completion of the work

q: A contractor seeks a secured advance against the entire value of the materials brought by him to the site of a work. The secured advance payable against such materials shall not ordinarily exceed:

options.A: 50% of the value of the materials
options.B: 75% of the value of the materials
options.C: 90% of the value of the materials
options.D: 100% of the value of the materials

q: A mobilisation advance is paid to a contractor at the commencement of a work. As regards interest on such an advance, the position under the contract is that it is:

options.A: An outright grant which is never recovered
options.B: Recovered only from the final bill of the work, without interest
options.C: Payable only after the completion of the work
options.D: Interest-bearing, the interest being recovered along with the advance from the contractor's bills

q: At the commencement of a large work, a contractor asks for a mobilisation advance of one-fourth of the contract value. The advance ordinarily admissible to him is limited to:

options.A: 10% of the contract value
options.B: 25% of the contract value
options.C: 50% of the contract value
options.D: 5% of the contract value

q: A works contract names a sum as payable in case of its breach, and a breach occurs, though the exact loss suffered is not precisely proved. Under Section 74 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, the party complaining of the breach is entitled to:

options.A: Nothing, unless the exact loss is proved to the last rupee
options.B: Twice the amount so named as compensation
options.C: Reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount so named, even though the actual loss is not precisely proved
options.D: Compensation only if the contract is registered

q: Due notice is given to a contractor to attend the recording of measurements of a work, but neither he nor his representative turns up, and the measurements are recorded by the Engineer in his absence. Such measurements:

options.A: Have to be postponed indefinitely
options.B: Cannot be relied upon for payment at all
options.C: Are recorded again by the contractor later at his convenience
options.D: Are binding on the contractor

q: A station building requires complete re-roofing and renewal of its flooring. These are heavy periodical repairs, not day-to-day maintenance, and they are treated as:

options.A: Ordinary repairs met from the day-to-day maintenance grant
options.B: Special repairs, executed under separately sanctioned estimates
options.C: Capital works in all cases
options.D: Deposit works of the occupying department

q: Lifts, escalators and air-conditioning plants installed in railway premises have to be maintained year after year. Such maintenance is commonly arranged through:

options.A: Annual Maintenance Contracts, often with the original equipment manufacturer or its authorised agency
options.B: Zonal contracts for petty works
options.C: Deposit works executed by the State PWD
options.D: The Workshop Manufacturing Suspense

q: A work sanctioned earlier is given up after part execution, leaving expenditure already incurred on the part work. That net infructuous expenditure is dealt with by:

options.A: Carrying it forward indefinitely under a suspense head
options.B: Recovering it from the contractor who executed the part work
options.C: Writing it off with the sanction of the competent authority, after taking over or disposing of the useful materials and assets created
options.D: Charging it to the next work sanctioned in the division

q: In the track renewal programme of a division, the item abbreviated as TRR refers to:

options.A: Total Rail Replacement
options.B: Track Repair and Renewal
options.C: Temporary Rail Restoration
options.D: Through Rail Renewal

q:
Consider the following statements about renewals of track components:
1. Piecemeal renewals of rails or sleepers at scattered locations, taken up as and when the need arises, are known as casual renewals.
2. In a through renewal, the track components are renewed over a continuous length of track in one operation.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: The ballast cushion under a track has become fouled with fines and dirt. Deep screening of the ballast is undertaken in such a case in order to:

options.A: Restore the elasticity and drainage of the ballast cushion by removing the accumulated fines and dirt
options.B: Increase the depth of the ballast cushion beyond the standard profile
options.C: Replace the stone ballast with cinder ballast
options.D: Test the quality of new ballast supplied by contractors

q: Bridge inspections are carried out every year on a division. The notes recorded at those inspections are entered in:

options.A: The Measurement Book of the section
options.B: The Bridge Register maintained for the purpose
options.C: The Works Register of the division
options.D: The Contractor's Ledger

q: At an important bridge, a 'danger level' is marked to show the flood level beyond which trains cannot be allowed freely. That level indicates the flood level at which:

options.A: The bridge falls due for painting
options.B: The bridge is to be closed permanently
options.C: Train traffic over the bridge must be stopped or regulated till the water recedes
options.D: Toll begins to be collected from road vehicles

q: Provision of proper drainage along the railway formation is insisted upon in works execution because:

options.A: It increases the permissible speed of trains on the section
options.B: It reduces the cost of ballast required for the track
options.C: It is required only in hilly sections of the railway
options.D: A water-logged formation loses its bearing capacity and leads to track defects and failures

q: While the annual track renewal programme is drawn up, the works to be included in it are selected primarily on the basis of:

options.A: The age-cum-condition of the track components and the gross million tonnes (GMT) of traffic carried over them
options.B: The age of the divisional office building
options.C: Representations received from the travelling public
options.D: The availability of surplus funds at the end of the year

q: A road over-bridge is proposed in place of a level crossing. In the Works Programme classification, bridge works of this kind fall under Plan Head:

options.A: 31 — Track Renewals
options.B: 32 — Bridge Works
options.C: 16 — Traffic Facilities
options.D: 30 — Road Safety Works (ROB/RUB)

q: A proposed work does not fit under any of the specific Plan Heads of the Works Programme. It is then classified under Plan Head:

options.A: 11 — New Lines (Construction)
options.B: 73 — Miscellaneous Advances
options.C: 64 — Other Specified Works
options.D: 81 — Metropolitan Transport Projects

q: At the site of an engineering work, one official supervises the execution directly and records the measurements of the work in the first instance. That official is the:

options.A: Assistant Engineer of the division
options.B: Divisional Railway Manager
options.C: Finance member of the tender committee
options.D: Inspector of Works / Section Engineer (Works) in charge of the section

q: For planning a major project and keeping watch over its progress, the construction organisation resorts to network techniques. CPM and PERT are used on the Railways for:

options.A: Planning, scheduling and monitoring the progress of major projects
options.B: Fixing the rates of items in the schedule of rates
options.C: Preparing the Pink Book of the Railway
options.D: Calculating the liquidated damages payable by a contractor

q: A bridge is described in two parts — the superstructure above and the supporting part below it. The supporting part, called the substructure, comprises:

options.A: The girders and the deck slab of the bridge
options.B: The foundations, piers and abutments which support the bridge girders
options.C: The track and fittings laid over the bridge
options.D: The approaches to the bridge

q: Revenue-charged petty works and repairs in a division are not normally entrusted to the construction organisation. They are ordinarily executed by:

options.A: The Construction organisation of the Railway
options.B: The Railway Board directly
options.C: The open line (maintenance) organisation of the division
options.D: A public sector undertaking on nomination

q: Two zonal railways settle a transaction between them in cash by financial adjustment, rather than through transfer transactions in the accounts. Such transactions are known as:

options.A: IRCA transactions
options.B: IRFA transactions
options.C: Suspense transactions
options.D: Remittance transactions

q: Before tenders for a work are called, certain preliminaries must be complete. Ordinarily, tenders should be invited only after:

options.A: The work has been physically started at the site
options.B: A suitable contractor has been identified informally
options.C: The completion report of the work has been prepared
options.D: Administrative approval and technical sanction have been accorded and the availability of funds for the work is ensured

q: When budgetary support under the Capital head is inadequate for capital works, the Railways draw upon a separate fund for such works. The Capital Fund is utilised mainly for:

options.A: Financing capital works chargeable to Capital, such as capacity-augmentation works, when budgetary support under the Capital head is inadequate
options.B: Meeting the ordinary working expenses of the Railways
options.C: Payment of dividend to General Revenues
options.D: Financing the ordinary repairs of buildings and track

q: A railway electrification project is included in the Works Programme. Its Plan Head classification is:
Rolling stock is taken from the Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC) on lease, and the lease charges have a capital component. That capital component is charged to Plan Head:

options.B: 22 (Leased Assets)

q: An officer holds a sanction for expenditure on a work, but no budget allotment has been made for it. The sanction by itself does not authorise him to incur the expenditure unless:

options.A: The tender for the work has been accepted
options.B: The work has been completed and taken over
options.C: The completion report has been vetted by Finance
options.D: Funds for the purpose have been allotted in the budget

q: At the close of the financial year, a division still holds an unspent balance of the grant allotted to it. That balance:

options.A: Lapses, and is not available for expenditure in the next year without a fresh allotment
options.B: Is automatically carried forward to the next year
options.C: Is transferred to the Development Fund
options.D: Can be spent in April of the next year without any sanction

q: A works contract contains a clause for the settlement of disputes by arbitration. For such an arbitration agreement to be valid under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, it must be:

options.A: Registered with the district court
options.B: Approved by the Railway Board in each case
options.C: In writing
options.D: Oral, provided it is made before two witnesses

q: A project for metropolitan transport in a metropolitan city is taken up by the Railways. In the Works Programme, it is classified under Plan Head:

options.A: 64 — Other Specified Works
options.B: 81 — Metropolitan Transport Projects
options.C: 11 — New Lines (Construction)
options.D: 16 — Traffic Facilities

q: Activities such as cleaning of trains and stations, catering services and linen management are not core railway functions and are got done through outside agencies. They are commonly executed through:

options.A: Deposit works executed for outside bodies
options.B: Zonal works contracts in all cases
options.C: Departmental execution in all cases
options.D: Services contracts governed by the General Conditions of Contract for Services

q: After the tenders for a work have been opened, a request is made to relax the qualifying criteria in favour of the lowest bidder. Such a course is not permissible because the eligibility criteria laid down in the tender documents:

options.A: Cannot be relaxed or changed after the opening of tenders
options.B: Can be relaxed after the opening of tenders in favour of the lowest tenderer
options.C: Can be modified by the Engineer after the opening of tenders
options.D: Are applicable only to contractors who are Government undertakings

q: After a works contract has been concluded, a change in its terms and conditions is proposed. Such an amendment to the concluded contract can be made only with:

options.A: The verbal approval of the Engineer at the site
options.B: The consent of the contractor alone
options.C: The approval of the authority competent to accept the tender, with the concurrence of Finance where required
options.D: The approval of the bank which issued the performance guarantee

q: Land has been acquired for a new railway work and its cost has to be accounted for. The cost of the land so acquired is:

options.A: Charged to Revenue in all cases
options.B: Charged to the same head and fund as the work for which the land is acquired, and forms part of the cost of that work
options.C: Borne by the State Government in all cases
options.D: Held permanently under a suspense head

q: A project executed by the Construction organisation of a zonal railway has been completed. The completed work is then taken over by:

options.A: The Railway Board
options.B: The Finance branch of the zonal railway
options.C: The Stores department of the zonal railway
options.D: The Open Line organisation, along with completion drawings and details of the assets created

q: Stores bought for stock are held in the depots of a railway. In the accounts, the value of the stores so held in stock is carried under the suspense head classified as:

options.A: Plan Head 71 — Stores Suspense
options.B: Plan Head 72 — Manufacturing Suspense
options.C: Plan Head 73 — Miscellaneous Suspense
options.D: Plan Head 64 — Other Specified Works

q:
Consider the following statements about the accounts of assets:
1. Where an entirely new asset is created and no asset existed before, its cost is booked on Additional Account.
2. Where an existing asset is renewed or replaced, its cost is booked on Replacement Account.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Works relating to railway research on the Railways are classified under Plan Head:

options.A: Plan Head 16 — Traffic Facilities
options.B: Plan Head 17 — Computerisation
options.C: Plan Head 21 — Rolling Stock
options.D: Plan Head 18 — Railway Research

q: Lease charges are paid to the Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC) for rolling stock taken on lease, and the charges include an interest element. That interest component is charged to:

options.A: Plan Head 22 — Leased Assets
options.B: Revenue, as part of the working expenses
options.C: Capital, along with the cost of the assets
options.D: Depreciation Reserve Fund

q: The high-speed rail project between Mumbai and Ahmedabad is not executed by a zonal railway directly. It is being executed by:

options.A: National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL)
options.B: Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL)
options.C: Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL)
options.D: Indian Railway Construction International Limited (IRCON)

q: Major railway projects are now planned in integration with the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan. That plan primarily provides:

options.A: A fund for financing railway projects through market borrowings
options.B: A GIS-based platform for coordinated and integrated planning of infrastructure projects
options.C: A tribunal for resolving disputes in infrastructure contracts
options.D: A scheme for subsidising freight rates on new lines

q: With the consent of all the parties, an existing contract is replaced by a fresh contract and the old contract is extinguished. This substitution of a contract is known as:

options.A: Grant of extension of the period of completion
options.B: Subletting of a portion of the work to another agency
options.C: Levy of liquidated damages for delayed completion
options.D: Substitution of a new contract in place of the existing contract, with the consent of all the parties, whereby the old contract is extinguished

q: The manual laying down the permanent way practices of the Railways is abbreviated IRPWM, which stands for:

options.A: Indian Railways Permanent Works Manual
options.B: Indian Railway Projects and Works Manual
options.C: Indian Railways Permanent Way Manual
options.D: Indian Railways Plant and Workshop Manual

q: Around the foundations of a bridge in a river, the bed is seen to have been eroded and lowered by the flow of water. This phenomenon, known as 'scour', refers to:

options.A: The erosion and lowering of the river bed around the foundations of a bridge due to the flow of water
options.B: The painting of steel girders with protective paint
options.C: The deposition of silt on the bed of the river
options.D: The development of cracks in the masonry of a bridge

q: An officer wants to consult the codified rules on the preparation and sanction of estimates and on tenders and contracts for engineering works. Those rules are contained in:

options.A: The Indian Railways Works Manual
options.B: The Indian Railways Code for the Engineering Department (Engineering Code)
options.C: The Indian Railways Stores Code
options.D: The Indian Railways Commercial Manual

q: The Pink Book is issued in two parts. Part I of the Pink Book (Works Programme) lists the works which are sanctioned by:

options.A: The General Manager under his delegated powers
options.B: The Divisional Railway Manager
options.C: The Ministry of Finance
options.D: The Railway Board

q: Panels of rails welded into long lengths in the track are referred to as LWR. The abbreviation stands for:

options.A: Long Welded Rail
options.B: Light Welded Rail
options.C: Local Welded Rail
options.D: Long Width Rail

q: For the purpose of internal check, the Accounts office keeps a register in which the sanctions accorded by competent authorities to estimates and to expenditure are recorded. That register is known as the:

options.A: Works Register
options.B: Liability Register
options.C: Register of Sanctions
options.D: Contractor's Ledger

q: A public-private partnership structure in which the private partner designs, builds, finances and operates the facility before transferring it is abbreviated DBFOT, which stands for:

options.A: Design, Bid, Finance, Operate and Terminate
options.B: Develop, Build, Fund, Own and Transfer
